stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy wants to hire a warehouse assistant who will work beside the controlled-substance cage. Eleven years ago his own registration was revoked for a regulatory violation; he has worked without incident since. The pharmacy proposes to hire him and document the history. What does the regulation permit?

choices.text: Hiring is permitted, because eleven incident-free years have passed.
Hiring is permitted if the pharmacy keeps him away from the cage itself.
Hiring is permitted once the Commissioner is notified of the history.
Hiring is barred, because a revoked registration disqualifies him at any time.
Hiring is barred unless a second registrant vouches for his trustworthiness.

explanation.core_reasoning: 105 CMR 700.005(B)(2) provides that NO REGISTRANT SHALL KNOWINGLY EMPLOY any agent or employee who has had an application for registration denied for violation of any law or regulation, or has had their registration REVOKED for violation of any law or regulation, AT ANY TIME. The bar carries no look-back period and no cure.

choice_analysis.A: The words at any time exclude a look-back limit.
choice_analysis.B: The screening duty reaches those who work in or around such areas.
choice_analysis.C: Notification is not a route around the bar.

related_facts: Screening documentation must be available to the Commissioner on request
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates assume an old regulatory event fades, as it would under many licensing schemes.

reasoning_steps: Note the absence of any look-back limit
Treat the prohibition as absolute rather than rebuttable
